tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H2): Bulk-plane conv and coalesced weight pass in K1 for the W=7/14/449x7 rows; interleaved 8,768 path check; 10-round precision log. Step 0: build the parent and the r0 anchor in your container and time them interleaved x3 (run_tests, not a ctypes harness); also time r3-a-e1-mma-fused-3launch's 8,768 path against the parent's library path at 8,768 interleaved x3 and report which is faster (the merge chose the custom path from a 62.4-vs-63.1 difference and reads 83.8 vs 80.1 on the portal). Step 1: replace k1_dw's 4-byte cp.async staging for the rows with W=7, W=14 and 449x7 (2/8/16/32,768,7,7; 8/16,384,14,14; 1,160,449,7) by a bulk-plane conv, re-implemented from the lineage D conclusion: one 1-D cp.async.bulk per group of channel planes (32 planes of 196 B = 6272 B for 7x7; whole 784 B planes for 14x14; 4-channel 50 KB groups for 449x7; every group is 16-B aligned and a multiple of 16 B) into zero-padded smem, one thread per 7-output row segment with the 49 taps in registers, LN partials (sum, sumsq) per token reduced in smem, d written channels-last fp16 as the parent's GEMM1 expects. Issue all plane copies for a CTA's work up front (mbarrier expect_tx), issue every tap load before the first FMA. Step 2: replace the role-CTA weight prep by a coalesced fp32->fp16 conversion of W1'=W1*lnw (and u, c1, b2') and W2 spread over ALL K1 CTAs as a first round (16-B loads and stores, 2+ CTAs/SM), so the 19 MB read + 9.5 MB write at C=768 (about 4-6 us) overlaps the conv CTAs; keep the TT layout cuBLASLt already accepts. Step 3: per-launch harness_time of K1 at 2,768, 8,768, 32,768, 16,384 and 1,160 old vs new in one container x3; record the conv-only and weight-only ablations. Step 4: run_tests all 16 rows with the parent as same-build control; for every row log over the harness's 10 seeded rounds (seed 200) against an fp64 reference the max |err| and the count of elements beyond that row's OWN atol + 1e-5|ref|; any row with a beyond-atol element gets the hi/lo fp16 split of the cheap operand before shipping. Step 5 (only if time remains, separate kernel, same hypothesis family): run the critic's probe for H29: K2 alone at 64,96 and 32,128 vs a plain read+write copy of the same bytes after the flush. Report per-row rented times with the per-path portal ratio (1.16-1.22 small rows, 1.23-1.32 others) and the projected score. Success: K1 drops by >= 8 us rented at 8,768 and >= 12 us at 32,768 in the interleaved comparison, with run_tests 16/16 and the 10-round precision log showing 0 elements beyond each row's own atol on every shipped path; total per-row gains of 8-20 us on at least five of the seven W=7/14/449x7 rows (projected >= +0.010 of mean at the per-path ratio). Refuted if: K1 at 32,768 loses less than 6 us rented, or the coalesced weight pass alone exceeds 8 us at C=768 and cannot be overlapped with the conv CTAs (then the weight conversion, not the conv staging, bounds K1 and the TF32-map route H14 is the follow-up). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE: in r3-merge-a3-b3-d3 the 8,768 row runs A3's LIBRARY path (A3's kCfg has use=0 at 8,768,7,7), not the custom mma.sync path; the portal 83.8 vs 80.1 us difference is within the portal's +-4% per-submission speed noise unless your interleaved step 0 shows otherwise.

Experiment E2 (tests H27): Counter-released dataflow replaces the two grid barriers in the cooperative kernel (S rows): microbench first, then build. Step 0: parent and r0 anchor interleaved x3 in your container (run_tests). Step 1 microbench (the critic's test plus I1's, 296 CTAs x 256 threads, 2xL2 flush before each launch, globaltimer): (a) release-to-observe latency when one CTA does red.release.gpu on a flag and 295 CTAs poll it with ld.acquire (one poller thread per CTA, no nanosleep; also a variant with ld.relaxed polling plus fence.acq_rel after the flip); (b) the same with 8 flags spread over separate 128-B lines, each polled by 37 CTAs; (c) the existing flip barrier (3000-3600 clk) and a two-level barrier (per-die or 8-line counter tree, final arriver writes per-group release flags) for reference. Report median and max clk per variant. Kill criterion for the dataflow build: if the best flag release-to-observe exceeds 1.2 us (about 2300 clk at 1.9 GHz) there is nothing to gain and you stop after shipping the best barrier variant into the parent instead. Step 2 (if the microbench passes): in the parent's ring path, (i) spread the conv units over all CTAs (at 1,192 it runs on 48 of 296, P1 median 1.8 us vs max 8.6); (ii) replace grid sync 1 by per-token-tile ready counters in a torch.empty int32 workspace: each conv CTA, after its d16 and LN-partial stores and a __threadfence/fence.proxy.async as needed, does one red.release.gpu.add per token tile it completed; each GEMM1 tile polls (one thread, ld.acquire, then __syncthreads) until its tile's count reaches the number of channel groups for this shape, then proceeds; (iii) replace grid sync 2 by per-image counters that GEMM1 tiles increment after their hidden and sumsq stores; GEMM2 tiles of image b poll for image b's GEMM1 tile count, so for B >= 2 images overlap; (iv) counters are monotone within a call and reset by the last GEMM2 tile of each image (or carry a per-call generation computed on the host from a module-level call counter is NOT allowed: use in-kernel reset by the last arriver, verified correct for every call and every order). Keep the cooperative launch (grid <= resident capacity, checked with cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor) so every producer is resident; order each CTA's static work list conv tiles -> GEMM1 tiles (image-major) -> GEMM2 tiles (image-major) so no CTA waits on work scheduled later in another CTA's list. Step 3: globaltimer stamps at 1,192 and 2,96 (P1 end median/max, first GEMM1 tile start, first GEMM2 tile start, end) old vs new. Step 4: run_tests all 16 rows with the parent as same-build control, dispatch per row only where the new path wins by > 1.5 us; log the 10-seeded-round per-row max |err| and beyond-own-atol counts for every B path (seed 200, fp64 reference). Report per-row times with the B ratio 1.24-1.26 and the projected score. Success: 1,192 <= 24 us rented and at least four of {1,96; 1,160; 2,96; 4,192; 4,96; 8,192} improve by >= 4 us against the same-build parent, 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-own-atol elements over the 10 seeded rounds on every shipped B path (projected >= +0.008 of mean). Refuted if: The best flag release-to-observe latency in the microbench exceeds 1.2 us, or the built dataflow kernel beats the parent by less than 2 us at 1,192 and 2,96 with the conv spread over all CTAs; then the cooperative S-row thesis is retired in r5 and its rows go to A or an E-lineage fused design. OPERATOR NOTE (correctness under the rules): torch.empty memory is uninitialised and can hold any earlier tensor's bytes (the caching allocator often hands back last call's block, so tests can pass by luck and then deadlock on the portal). Counters that must start at zero therefore cannot live in a torch.empty workspace unless the same call zeroes them before any CTA can poll them, which needs an ordering point. Self-resetting counters belong in a module-level device buffer allocated once (cudaMalloc + cudaMemset to zero on first use, sized for the largest shape); the ledger allows this as 'a scratch counter that is correct for every call'. The last arriver must restore every counter it uses to zero so the next call, of any shape and in any order, starts clean. Prove it: run_tests with the portal-order check, plus one probe run where the torch.empty workspace is deliberately filled with 0xFF before the launch to show nothing depends on its initial contents.

Experiment E3 (tests H28): tcgen05 kind::f16 swap-AB engine inside D's cooperative wide-C kernel, gated by a GEMM probe. Step 0: parent (v3) and r0 anchor interleaved x3 in your container. Gate probe (<= 1 hour): take the #35 tc_ws tcgen05 kind::f16 ring kernel from the archive (get_kernel; another problem's kernel, allowed as a structure reference and flagged to the operator) and run it unmodified on pre-converted fp16 operands after the 2xL2 flush for 1568x3072x768, 1568x768x3072 and 392x3072x768; also time one 128x208x768 single-CTA tile with an MN-major (token-contiguous) fp16 B operand from a [k][token] buffer against a K-major reference and check the accumulators are bit-identical. GO if each full GEMM is <= 6 us rented at the 1568 shapes and <= 3 us at 392 and the MN-major descriptor validates; KILL if any exceeds 10 us (then report and spend the session on the fallback: KC=64 chunks and a double-buffered fp16 B in the mma.sync ring to halve the per-chunk __syncthreads). Build (GO): keep D's skeleton (phase A bulk-plane conv writing d as fp16 [c][token] per image plus per-token LN partials, W conversion to fp16 L2 scratch by a first round over all CTAs or a TFLOAT32 map for W1 at 2,768 where MMA is 0.5 us, sync 1, GEMM1, sync 2, GEMM2 with coalesced red.add.v4 into out prefilled with x + W2*gb + b2 where KS > 1). Swap engine: cta_group::1 first (M = 128 weight rows), A = W tile K-major from fp16 scratch through a 128B-swizzled TMA ring, B = activations [channel][token] MN-major with N = tokens of one image (49 -> 64 padded by TMA OOB fill) or an image group (4 x 49 = 196 -> 208/256; one 14x14 image = 196), K = C then 4C, 128-k per stage (2 k-blocks) so each stage carries >= 600 clk of MMA; whole-warp TMA producer and MMA warp with elect.sync, full/empty mbarrier pairs, 4-6 stages, TMEM allocated once per CTA. GEMM1 epilogue: tcgen05.ld, thread owns hidden channel k and 32 token columns per load; LN fold z = rstd[t]*(acc - mu[t]*u[k]) + v[k] with mu/rstd from smem, exact erff GELU, fp16 hidden to L2 as [k][token] via 16-B stores, per-(image,k) sumsq as in-thread sums (no atomics within a tile; one red.add per (image,k) only if a tile spans a partial image). After sync 2: s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*gf/mean computed once per image by the CTA that needs it with all gf loads issued first; GEMM2 A = W2 tile [128 c][K=4C], B = hidden [4C][tokens] MN-major, the GRN scale applied per K-row of the B stage by a 4-warp transform group after the TMA lands (fence.proxy.async before the MMA; the transform warps must have no global loads in flight when they arrive), or alternatively per column of the W2 A stage; pick by a per-stage clk measurement. Epilogue: acc [c][tokens] + x (16-B coalesced along hw) stored directly in NCHW, or red.add.v4 for split-K. Tile counts per row as multiples of 148 (or 74 pairs if you move to cta_group::2 later). Measure clk per stage in the MMA warp against the 2N-clk-per-64-k ideal and fix any ELECT/BRA.U.ANY waterfall in SASS. run_tests all 16 rows (other rows keep the parent's dispatch), 10-seeded-round per-row max |err| and beyond-own-atol log (fp64 reference) for every D path. Report per-row rented times with the D ratio ~1.32 and the projected score. Success: Gate passed and the built kernel reaches at least four of: 2,768 <= 32, 8,768 <= 45, 16,768 <= 55, 32,768 <= 75, 8,384 <= 45, 16,384 <= 60 us rented (same-build control), 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-own-atol elements over 10 seeded rounds (projected >= +0.02 of mean). Refuted if: The gate GEMMs exceed 10 us at the 1568 shapes, or the built kernel beats D v3 by less than 25% at 16,768 and 32,768, or its per-stage clk stays above 1.5x the MMA ideal after the waterfall fix; then wide-C rows move to a library-with-fused-epilogue route (CUTLASS EVT, pool I6/I8/I16) in r5.
